# Glycolic Acid vs Lactic Acid For Hyperpigmentation India: Which AHA Is Best For Dark Marks?

Deciding how to tackle your skin concerns? Choose Glycolic Acid (5%-10%) if your main skin concern is deep epidermal hyperpigmentation, stubbor Start your free skin analysis now on MyMirror. Clinical SEO Page Packet.

sections.heading: Quick Verdict
sections.markdown:
## Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

Choose Glycolic Acid (5%-10%) if your main skin concern is deep epidermal hyperpigmentation, stubborn sun spots, or coarse skin texture, provided your skin barrier is resilient. Choose Lactic Acid (5%-10%) if you have sensitive, dry, or melanin-dense skin prone to post-acne marks, as it offers gentle exfoliation with natural humectant hydration.

Quick Verdict: Which Active Ingredient Should You Pick?

sections.heading: Comparison Methodology
sections.markdown:
## Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

Glycolic Acid has the smallest molecular size (76.05 g/mol) among Alpha Hydroxy Acids, enabling deep epidermal penetration to break desmosome bonds. Lactic Acid has a larger molecular structure (90.08 g/mol) and inherent NMF humectant properties, exfoliating surface dead cells with minimal burning.

Dermatological Comparison & Action Mechanisms

sections.heading: Decision Criteria
sections.markdown:
## Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

Indian skin Fitzpatrick IV-VI has higher epidermal melanin density. High-concentration Glycolic Acid can trigger post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) if overused. Lactic Acid is preferred for sensitive or barrier-compromised skin.

Decision Criteria for Indian Skin Types

sections.heading: Side By Side Matrix
sections.markdown:
## Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

Glycolic Acid (5%-10%) offers deep exfoliation for resilient skin. Lactic Acid (5%-10%) offers gentle surface brightening and humectant hydration for sensitive melanin-rich skin.

| Parameter | Glycolic Acid (5%-10%) | Lactic Acid (5%-10%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Molecular Weight | Small (76.05 g/mol) | Medium (90.08 g/mol) |
| Penetration Depth | Deep Epidermal | Surface Epidermal |
| Primary Benefit | Rapid texture smoothing & mark fading | Gentle brightening & humectant hydration |
| Irritation Risk | Moderate (Initial tingling) | Low (Gentle on sensitive skin) |
| Best Skin Type | Oily / Resilient skin | Sensitive / Dry / Melanin-rich skin |

Side-by-Side Comparison Matrix

sections.heading: Reader Fit Tradeoffs
sections.markdown:
## How To Layer Both Actives Safely

Start with Lactic Acid 5% twice weekly in your PM routine. Transition to Glycolic Acid 5% once your barrier adapts. Always pair AHA exfoliation with daily broad-spectrum SPF 50 sunscreen.

How To Layer Both Actives Safely

sections.heading: Trust Proof
sections.markdown:
## Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

Reviewed by Board-Certified Dermatologists. Always perform a 24-hour patch test behind the ear before applying AHA exfoliants across your entire face.

Clinical Safety & Dermatologist Notes

sections.heading: Faq
sections.markdown:
### Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can Glycolic Acid cause dark spots? A: Yes, over-exfoliating melanin-rich skin with high % Glycolic Acid can trigger rebound PIH if sun protection is omitted. Q: Is Lactic Acid safe for sensitive skin? A: Yes, Lactic Acid is the gentlest AHA due to its larger molecular size.

Frequently Asked Questions
